sections.h2: Where is Pickens County and what towns does it have?
sections.html:
Pickens County is in the northwest corner of South Carolina and covers 512.75 square miles, of which 496.94 are land. The county seat is the city of Pickens, while Easley is the largest community.

Other municipalities include Liberty, Central, Clemson, Six Mile and Norris. Clemson takes in the former community of Calhoun.

  • Transylvania County, North Carolina lies to the north.
  • Greenville County is to the east and Anderson County to the south.
  • Oconee County, which was split off from Pickens in 1868, is on the west side.

Sassafras Mountain, the highest natural point in South Carolina at 3,560 feet, is inside the county. Table Rock State Park and Keowee-Toxaway State Park are also here, so sellers near the northern edge deal with a very different landscape than those in Easley.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Pickens County?
sections.html:
Pickens County was created in 1826, and the legislation took effect in 1828 once the state moved to judicial districts. It was named for Brigadier General Andrew Pickens, a Revolutionary War officer.

The local economy long rested on textiles and farming, with manufacturing growing after World War II. Historic sites such as Hagood Mill and Fort Hill, the former home of John C. Calhoun, still mark that earlier era.

sections.h2: What drives the Pickens County economy today?
sections.html:
Educational services lead employment in Pickens County at 21.4% of jobs in the third quarter of 2023, and Clemson University is the main reason. Accommodation and food services follow at 15.2%, retail trade at 15.0% and manufacturing at 13.5%.

Output in 2022 was about $5 billion, or roughly $37,089 per person. The county's profile lists Clemson University, Prisma Health, Walmart, Lowe's and Publix among its major employers.

sections.h2: When does Pickens County collect property tax?
sections.html:
The Pickens County Treasurer collects current property taxes from October 1 to March 16 each year, and January 15 is the last day to pay without penalty. Vehicle taxes are collected all year.

Mortgage escrow bills are mailed around October 1, and lenders normally pay by the end of December. Payments are dated by U.S. postmark.

  • Office: 222 McDaniel Avenue, B-6, Pickens, SC 29671, behind the County Health Department off Highway 178.
  • Hours: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
  • Phone: (864) 898-5883.
  • In person the office accepts cash, check or money order. By mail, send payment to the same street address and a receipt comes back.

The page does not list late fees, so use the statute: after January 15 a 3% penalty applies, then another 7% before February 2 and 5% before March 17 (S.C. Code 12-45-180).

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes in Pickens County?
sections.html:
Bills still open after the March 16 collection window end up with the county's Delinquent Tax Office, which is at 222 McDaniel Avenue, B-15, and can be reached at (864) 898-5890. Under S.C. Code 12-45-180, collection of unpaid bills then follows Chapter 51 of Title 12.

The county's tax sale process is handled through that office.

If you sell during this period, the buyer's title company will want a payoff figure that includes penalties and costs. Ask for it early, because it changes with each penalty date.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Pickens County assessment?
sections.html:
In a year with a Notice of Valuation, you must object in writing within 90 days after the Assessor mails it. In a year with no notice, you file before the first penalty date, and a filing before that date applies to the current tax year while a later one applies to the next.

  1. Informal review: a licensed appraiser looks at every timely appeal.
  2. Notice of Decision: the Assessor mails the result.
  3. Pickens County Board of Assessment Appeals: file written notice with the Assessor within 30 days of the decision date.
  4. Administrative Law Judge Division: appeal within 30 days of the Board's written decision.

Appeals cannot be faxed and must go to the Assessor, not another county office. An agent needs a signed authorization or power of attorney from the owner. The county warns that a missed deadline or a wrong filing can get an appeal dismissed. The Assessor's number is (864) 898-5872.

sections.h2: When does a sale trigger a reassessment in Pickens County?
sections.html:
A recorded deed can trigger a reassessment, even when no money changes hands. The Assessor calls this an Assessable Transfer of Interest, and it raises the value to fair market value as of December 31 of the year of transfer.

The last countywide reassessment took effect December 31, 2018, and appeared on 2019 notices. State law calls for a reappraisal every fifth year, and the Assessor must send a Notice of Valuation when value rises by $1,000 or more (S.C. Code 12-43-217). The Assessor's FAQ does not state the next reassessment year, so ask the office.

The owner on December 31 is liable for that year's tax, and the lien follows the property. The bill therefore follows the property, so a closing should settle it.

sections.h2: How does the 4% legal residence rate affect a Pickens County sale?
sections.html:
An owner-occupied primary home is assessed at 4%, and anything not owner-occupied is assessed at 6%. The application goes to the Assessor after the deed records and you move in, due before the first penalty date.

A transfer into a trust requires a new application. The 4% rate is removed for trust transfers unless the income beneficiary lives in the home as a primary residence and the trustee certifies it. If eligibility ends and you do not tell the Assessor within six months, the penalty can reach 100% of the tax paid plus interest.

Estate and rental sellers should check the status first. A rate that changed from 4% to 6% raises the bill the buyer will see.

Statewide, the deed recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, split $1.30 state and $0.55 county, and a deed in lieu of foreclosure is exempt (S.C. Code 12-24-10 and 12-24-40).

sections.h2: What do Pickens County sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Sellers here often hold an inherited house in Easley or Pickens, a rental near Clemson that has aged, or a mountain property that is hard to maintain. Several offices matter.

  • Treasurer, (864) 898-5883, for the current bill.
  • Auditor, (864) 898-5895, for personal property and homestead exemption questions.
  • Assessor, (864) 898-5872, for the rate and value.
  • Delinquent Tax, (864) 898-5890, for anything past March 16.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in their current condition, so a seller with an older or damaged house does not need to repair it first. Call the offices above, get the numbers, and then compare them with what a buyer offers.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Pickens County SC property taxes?
faqs.a: January 15 is the last day to pay without penalty. The Treasurer collects current taxes from October 1 to March 16.

faqs.q: Where is the Pickens County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 222 McDaniel Avenue, B-6, Pickens, SC 29671, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday. The phone number is (864) 898-5883.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Pickens County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written objection with the Assessor within 90 days of the Notice of Valuation. If you disagree with the decision, you can go to the County Board of Assessment Appeals within 30 days, then to the Administrative Law Judge Division.

faqs.q: Does selling a house reassess it in Pickens County?
faqs.a: Yes, a recorded deed can trigger an Assessable Transfer of Interest. The value is raised to fair market value as of December 31 of the transfer year.

faqs.q: Who do I call about delinquent taxes in Pickens County?
faqs.a: Call the Delinquent Tax Office at (864) 898-5890. It is located at 222 McDaniel Avenue, B-15, Pickens.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pickens County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the tax from the proceeds at closing, and Cash Home Buyers can buy the house as it is.
